title: Madeleines
summary: Light, lemon-scented French sponge cakes baked in a shell-shaped tin, prized for the signature domed hump that forms as cold batter meets a hot oven.
equipment: madeleine tin(s), metal, 12-hole (bake in 2 batches if you have one)
bowl and whisk or stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled until warm

steps.title: Whisk eggs and sugar
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, caster sugar, honey, lemon zest and salt together for 4-5 minutes, until pale, thick and roughly doubled in volume. This long whisking stage builds the air bubbles that give madeleines their light sponge.

steps.title: Fold in flour
steps.text: Sift the flour and baking powder over the whisked mixture and fold in gently. Folding, rather than stirring vigorously, keeps the air you've just whisked in from collapsing.

steps.title: Fold in butter
steps.text: Fold in the warm melted butter in two additions, mixing until glossy. Adding it warm helps it combine evenly without weighing down the batter.

steps.title: Chill the batter
steps.text: Cover and chill the batter for at least 1 hour, and up to 2 days. A cold, rested batter meeting a hot oven is exactly what produces the signature humped back on a madeleine.

steps.title: Prepare the metal tin
steps.text: Brush the moulds of the metal madeleine tin with soft butter, dust with flour and tap out the excess, then chill the tin. A metal tin heats quickly and evenly, and this buttered-and-floured coating helps each cake turn out cleanly with sharp shell markings.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking. A properly hot oven creates the sharp contrast in temperature that drives the hump.

steps.title: Fill and bake
steps.text: Spoon 1 level tablespoon of cold batter into each mould, filling them about three-quarters full, without spreading it out. Bake for 9-11 minutes, until humped, golden at the edges, and the tops spring back when lightly pressed.

steps.title: Unmould and repeat
steps.text: Tap the madeleines out of the tin straight away onto a wire rack, as they stick if left to cool in the moulds. Re-butter and flour the tin, then repeat with any remaining chilled batter.

steps.title: Dust and serve
steps.text: Dust the cooled madeleines with icing sugar just before serving. They're at their best within a few hours of baking, while the edges are still a little crisp.

tips: Don't skip chilling the batter - baking it straight away, without the cold-to-hot contrast, is the main reason madeleines come out flat instead of humped.
Fill the moulds only three-quarters full; overfilling stops them humping properly and can make them spill over.
Turn them out immediately after baking, as leaving madeleines in the tin even a minute or two can cause them to stick.
Keep spare batter chilled between batches so later madeleines hump just as well as the first tray.
Dust with icing sugar only just before serving, as it will dissolve into the cake if left to sit.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten within a few hours of baking. Any extra can be kept in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or frozen for up to 1 month; warm gently before serving to bring back their softness.
